denomProfiles/episcopal-church-usa/tagli: American Anglicanism: Prayer Book worship, democratic polity and progressive social stances.
denomProfiles/episcopal-church-usa/coreD: The Book of Common Prayer (1979) as the main expression of its faith.
Holy Scripture, the creeds, the sacraments and the historic episcopate (the Chicago Quadrilateral, 1886).
Baptism as full initiation into the Body of Christ, with a Baptismal Covenant.
Full inclusion of women and LGBTQ people in all orders; marriage rites for same-sex couples since 2015.
The Thirty-nine Articles kept as 'historical documents'.
denomProfiles/episcopal-church-usa/focus: Social justice, racial reconciliation and the 'Jesus Movement' language of Michael Curry.
Ecumenical full communion with the ELCA (2001) and others.
Prayer Book worship and church music.
Dioceses beyond the US, in Latin America, Taiwan and Europe.
denomProfiles/episcopal-church-usa/pract: The Eucharist as the principal Sunday service.
Bishops elected by diocesan conventions; a triennial General Convention with houses of bishops and deputies.
Women priests since 1976 and bishops since 1989.
Infant and adult baptism; confirmation by a bishop.
denomProfiles/episcopal-church-usa/influ: Departing dioceses and congregations formed it in 2009.
The two churches entered full communion in 1961.
William Reed Huntington's proposal became the Anglican basis for church unity.
denomProfiles/episcopal-church-usa/keyFi: First Presiding Bishop and architect of the constitution.
denomProfiles/episcopal-church-usa/membe: About 1.6 million baptised members reported in parochial reports for 2022 (Office of the General Convention); average Sunday attendance is far lower.
denomProfiles/church-of-nigeria/tagline: One of Anglicanism's largest provinces, evangelistic and theologically conservative.
denomProfiles/church-of-nigeria/coreDoct: Scripture as the final authority, with the Thirty-nine Articles and the Book of Common Prayer.
The Jerusalem Declaration (GAFCON, 2008) as a statement of orthodox Anglican faith.
Salvation through faith in Christ alone and the need for personal conversion.
Marriage as between one man and one woman; opposition to same-sex blessings.
Its 2005 constitution defines communion by 'the historic faith' rather than by the see of Canterbury.
denomProfiles/church-of-nigeria/focuses/: Evangelism and church planting, including missionary dioceses in the north.
Leadership of GAFCON and the conservative realignment in global Anglicanism.
Witness amid violence against Christians in northern and central Nigeria.
denomProfiles/church-of-nigeria/practice: Prayer Book worship in English, Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa and other languages, often with lively music.
Harvest thanksgiving, revival services and night vigils.
Strong Mothers' Union and youth fellowships.
Women serve in many lay ministries but are not ordained priests.
denomProfiles/church-of-nigeria/influenc: Its founder Josiah Oshitelu was an Anglican catechist.
Nigeria's Convocation of Anglicans in North America (2005) helped form it.
Archbishop Peter Akinola was a leader of the 2008 Jerusalem conference.
denomProfiles/church-of-nigeria/keyFigur: Primate (2000–10) and a founder of GAFCON.
denomProfiles/church-of-nigeria/members/: The church's own claim of about 18 million members, widely repeated in the 2000s and 2010s but not independently verified.
denomProfiles/anglican-church-of-kenya/t: Revival-shaped Kenyan Anglicanism with a strong voice in national public life.
denomProfiles/anglican-church-of-kenya/c: Scripture, the creeds and the historic Anglican formularies.
Evangelical emphasis on repentance, new birth and assurance shaped by the East African Revival.
The Jerusalem Declaration (2008) as an affirmation of orthodox Anglicanism.
Marriage between one man and one woman.
Ordination of women as priests and bishops.
denomProfiles/anglican-church-of-kenya/f: Public theology, including criticism of political abuses in the 1980s and 1990s.
Education, from mission schools to St Paul's University, Limuru.
Development and health work through church agencies.
denomProfiles/anglican-church-of-kenya/p: Worship from Our Modern Services (2002) in English and Swahili and local languages.
Revival fellowship meetings with public testimony.
Women priests since 1983 and women bishops since 2021.
Large youth and Mothers' Union movements.
denomProfiles/anglican-church-of-kenya/i: Kenyan archbishops hosted the 2013 Nairobi conference and chaired the movement.
Bishops such as David Gitari shaped debates over democracy and multiparty politics.
denomProfiles/anglican-church-of-kenya/k: CMS pioneer missionary at Mombasa and Rabai.
Archbishop (1997–2002) known for prophetic preaching against injustice.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/tagline: Church of the Uganda Martyrs and the East African Revival.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/coreDoctr: Scripture and the Anglican formularies, with an evangelical emphasis.
Salvation through the cross of Christ; 'walking in the light' through confession.
Remembrance of the martyrs of 1885–87 as witnesses to Christ.
Marriage between one man and one woman.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/focuses/1: Education, including Uganda Christian University at Mukono.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/focuses/3: Speaking on public affairs, notably under Idi Amin.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/practices: Annual Martyrs' Day pilgrimage to Namugongo (3 June), shared with Catholics.
Revival hymn 'Tukutendereza Yesu' and public testimony by the Balokole ('saved ones').
Prayer Book worship in Luganda, English and other languages.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/influence: The revival spread from Uganda and Rwanda into Kenya.
Uganda gave oversight to US congregations before ACNA formed.
Balokole fellowships spread into Tanzania, Rwanda and beyond.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/keyFigure: CMS missionary and engineer in Buganda from 1878.
Evangelist to the Congo border region.
Lay leader of the East African Revival.
Archbishop murdered in 1977 after protesting abuses under Idi Amin.
Bishop and evangelist who preached forgiveness after exile.
denomProfiles/church-of-uganda/members/n: About a third of Uganda's population, some 11 million people, identified as Anglican in the 2014 national census (Uganda Bureau of Statistics).
denomProfiles/anglican-church-in-north-a: Conservative Anglicans in North America, aligned with GAFCON and the Global South.
Scripture as the inspired Word of God and the final authority.
The 1662 Book of Common Prayer, the Ordinal and the Thirty-nine Articles as standards.
The Jerusalem Declaration (2008).
Marriage between one man and one woman.
Bishops are men; dioceses decide whether to ordain women priests.
Church planting across the United States and Canada.
Catechesis through To Be a Christian (2014, rev. 2020).
Communion with GAFCON and Global South provinces.
Holding evangelical, Anglo-Catholic and charismatic streams together.
The Book of Common Prayer 2019.
Diocesan and network structures, with a College of Bishops electing the archbishop.
Women ordained deacons, and priests in some dioceses.
Weekly Eucharist with varied worship styles.
Global Anglican realignment
Its recognition by GAFCON primates modelled an alternative to Canterbury-centred structures.
Robert Duncan
First Archbishop (2009–14).
Foley Beach
Archbishop (2014–24).
Steve Wood
Archbishop elected in 2024.
J. I. Packer
Theologian and general editor of its catechism.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/tagl: The first union of episcopal and non-episcopal churches, born in 1947.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/core: Scripture as the supreme and decisive standard of faith.
The Apostles' and Nicene Creeds as witness to the faith.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments.
The historic episcopate in a constitutional, synodical form.
Recognition of the ministries of all uniting churches without reordination.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/focu: Education and health care, with many schools, colleges and hospitals.
Women's leadership: women ordained from 1976 and bishops from 2013.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/prac: CSI liturgy (1950) and Book of Common Worship, used in Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Telugu and English.
Synod led by an elected Moderator; about two dozen dioceses.
Festivals such as harvest festivals and Christmas carol rounds.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/infl: The 1970 northern union followed its path.
Lesslie Newbigin's defence of the scheme shaped union debates worldwide.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/keyF: Bishop of Dornakal and pioneer of the union.
Bishop of Madurai–Ramnad and theologian of the union.
Bishop of Coimbatore and Indian Christian theologian.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/memb: The church's own figure of about four million members; not verified by census.
denomProfiles/church-of-south-india/inIn: Formed at St George's Cathedral, Madras, on 27 September 1947, it is one of India's largest Protestant churches, strongest in Tamil Nadu (Tirunelveli, Kanyakumari, Madurai, Chennai) and Kerala, with dioceses also in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Jaffna in Sri Lanka.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/tagl: A broad union of six churches, including Baptists and Brethren, formed in 1970.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/core: Scripture as the supreme rule of faith, with the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper; both infant and believers' baptism are recognised.
The historic episcopate, accepted with a unification of ministries at the inauguration.
Full communion with Anglican, Methodist and Reformed world bodies.
Commitment to the unity of the Church as a sign for India.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/focu: Ministry among Dalit and Adivasi communities and in the north-east.
Interfaith dialogue in a religiously plural society.
Advocacy for the rights of religious minorities.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/prac: Synod with an elected Moderator and over two dozen dioceses.
Liturgies drawing on Anglican, Methodist and Reformed traditions in Hindi and regional languages.
Parents may choose infant baptism or later believers' baptism.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/infl: Church of Pakistan and Church of Bangladesh
The same plan of union produced the Church of Pakistan (1970), from which the Church of Bangladesh separated after 1971.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/keyF: Metropolitan of the Church of India, Pakistan, Burma and Ceylon during the union negotiations.
Baptist pioneer whose mission's heirs joined the union.
Church of Scotland educationist whose mission fed into the United Church of Northern India.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/memb: The church's own figure of about 2.2 million members; not verified by census.
denomProfiles/church-of-north-india/inIn: Inaugurated at Nagpur on 29 November 1970, it serves northern, central, western and north-eastern India, with large communities in Punjab, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and the north-east.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/ta: Canada's largest Protestant church: a 1925 union with a progressive social witness.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/co: The Basis of Union (1925), with later statements including A Song of Faith (2006).
Jesus Christ as the centre of faith, with Scripture as the church's primary source.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments.
Full inclusion of LGBTQ people in membership and ministry (1988).
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/fo: Social justice and the Social Gospel tradition.
Reconciliation with Indigenous peoples, including apologies in 1986 and 1998.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/pr: Worship with hymns from Voices United (1996) and More Voices.
Government by councils (community, regional and General Council since 2019).
Infant baptism and an open table.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/in: Its 1925 union across Methodist, Presbyterian and Congregational lines became a precedent for later unions.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/ke: Methodist general superintendent and union advocate.
Medical missionary and first lay Moderator (1968).
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/me: About 1.2 million people identified with the United Church in Statistics Canada's 2021 census; formal membership is much lower.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-canada/in: Its Presbyterian predecessor's Central India mission (from 1877, around Indore and Malwa) contributed congregations and institutions to the Church of North India.
